chunks.text: 56-year-old male, Associate Professional or Technician, resident of Ang Mo Kio, Singapore.
Fractured left humerus in 2010, fully healed
Completed course of amoxicillin for UTI in 2015
Elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy for symptomatic gallstones (elective).
General anesthesia with Laryngeal Mask Airway (LMA) and ultrasound-guided regional analgesia
General anesthesia for appendectomy in 2005, no complications

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr. Tan. I'm Dr. Liew from the anesthesia team. Today, we'll discuss your upcoming surgery and ensure you're ready for anesthesia. Let's start with your gallstones. How have they been affecting you?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Morning, doc. Been having this sharp pain on the right side, especially after eating fried food. Had to stop my chili crab lah. Also, felt nauseous a few times. Scans showed stones, so doctor said remove the gallbladder.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understood. Now, let's go through your medications. You're on amlodipine, metoprolol, atorvastatin, metformin, omeprazole, and aspirin. But I noticed the records say aspirin is still active. Have you stopped or changed any medications in the past year?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Oh, right! I stopped the aspirin about six months ago. Had some tummy bleeding, like black stools and all. Doctor said to stop it and switch to omeprazole for protection.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for clarifying that. So, aspirin was discontinued due to gastrointestinal bleeding. No other medication changes?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Nope, all others are still the same. Blood pressure and sugar are controlled, lah. HbA1c was 7.2% last check.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Any allergies to medications or foods?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: None that I know of. Never had a reaction before.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. You mentioned GERD earlier. Any recent acid reflux episodes or difficulty swallowing?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Sometimes at night if I eat late, but omeprazole helps. No problem swallowing food.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Noted. Have you eaten or drunk anything since midnight? We need to ensure your stomach is empty for anesthesia.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, doc. Had my last meal at 8pm last night. Just water this morning, but stopped at 6am.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect. Any previous surgeries or anesthesia? Reactions like difficulty waking up or nausea?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Appendectomy when I was younger. Anesthesia was smooth, no issues. Recovered well.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. Finally, how are your daily activities? Can you climb stairs or walk without discomfort?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No problem, doc. Walk 30 minutes most days. Only the gallstone pain stops me sometimes.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you, Mr. Tan. We'll proceed with general anesthesia using an LMA and regional analgesia as planned. The team will ensure your blood pressure and sugar are monitored closely. Any questions?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No questions, doc. Ready to get this done.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] induction propofol one hundred twenty milligrams, fentanyl fifty micrograms, rocuronium fifty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:02] LMA inserted, grade one view, capnography confirmed

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:03] mean arterial pressure dropped to sixty, atropine zero point five milligrams given intravenously

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] sixteen gauge peripheral line placed, blood pressure one hundred seventy over ninety

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] five hundred milliliters lactated Ringer's administered

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:15] ultrasound-guided transversus abdominis plane block performed with forty milliliters bupivacaine zero point five percent

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:20] heart rate increased to one hundred twenty, esmolol one milligram bolus administered

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi Mr. Tan, how are you feeling now after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I’m okay, got some pain here, but manageable.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Can you give me a pain score out of 10?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: About 4 or 5, not too bad.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Any nausea or feeling like you might vomit?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: A bit queasy, but didn’t throw up.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Any sore throat, cough, or breathing difficulties?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Slight sore throat, but breathing’s fine.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Do you remember anything from the operation?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Nope, everything’s blank.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Any issues with your blood pressure, blood sugar, or reflux since the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No dizziness or anything, but sometimes I get heartburn at night.

claims.text: 56-year-old male, resident of Ang Mo Kio, Singapore, undergoing elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy for symptomatic gallstones.
Diagnosed with type 2 diabetes; HbA1c 7.2% at last check, controlled with metformin 500mg twice daily.
Hypertension controlled on amlodipine 10mg daily and metoprolol 50mg twice daily; no current symptoms of heart disease.
No residual respiratory symptoms (e.g., chronic cough, wheeze, shortness of breath) from resolved pneumonia (2018).
No new medical conditions, surgeries, or hospitalizations since last anesthetic in 2005 except for resolved pneumonia (2018) and current gallstone disease.
Current medications: amlodipine 10mg daily, metoprolol 50mg twice daily, atorvastatin 20mg nightly, metformin 500mg twice daily, omeprazole 20mg daily.
Aspirin 75mg daily discontinued 6 months ago due to gastrointestinal bleeding; replaced with omeprazole 20mg daily for gastroprotection.
No known drug allergies.
NPO after midnight; last meal at 8pm, water until 6am.
No history of airway difficulties, intubation issues, or breathing problems during prior general anesthesia (appendectomy 2005).
ASA-PS III (controlled hypertension and diabetes without systemic impairment).

56-year-old male post-laparoscopic cholecystectomy with intraoperative hypotension requiring atropine, followed by hypertension (170/90 mmHg), and tachycardia (HR 120) treated with esmolol.

Elective surgery for gallstones. History of controlled type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 7.2%), hypertension (on amlodipine, metoprolol), and resolved pneumonia (2018). Current meds: metformin, amlodipine, metoprolol, atorvastatin, omeprazole. No prior airway issues. ASA-PS III. Anesthesia plan included LMA and TAP block with bupivacaine.

High PONV risk due to opioid use and gallstone-related nausea history. Hemodynamic instability noted intraoperatively. Requires glycemic monitoring for diabetes. Analgesia needs post-TAP block. Aspiration risk with LMA in context of possible GERD.

Administer PONV prophylaxis. Monitor BP and HR closely; consider antihypertensive if needed. Check blood glucose q2h. Continue current home medications (except held pre-op). Provide analgesia per protocol. Maintain LMA precautions for possible aspiration risk.
